messages.author: 25db316bc69e2c34
messages.subject: Constant environment in two-lump
parts:
Hello everyone,

I have been trying to use two-lump to model the effect of a variation of thermal property and thickness of the bony coverage of a few species of lizards. In a nutshell I am trying to obtain from two-limp what one-lump does but accounting for an external shell.
I am struggling to use constant values as input for climate variables (Tairf etc). I tried different approaches but I managed to get the furthest (I think) using something like  approxfun(df$time, c(rep(25, length(df$time), rule = 2) in the case of air temperature.
Still it doesn't seem to work and I receive the error message "Error in q * V : non-numeric argument to binary operator"

Is what I am trying to do something possible at all? Am I just misunderstanding how approxfun works?

This is a simplified example of my last attempt

Ww_g <- 40
alpha <- 0.7
time <- seq(0, 3500, 10)
Tradf <-approxfun(time, rep(26, length(time)), rule = 2)
velf <- approxfun(time, rep(0.01, length(time)), rule = 2)
Tairf <- approxfun(time, rep(25, length(time)), rule = 2)
Zenf <- approxfun(time, rep(0, length(time)), rule = 2)
Qsolf <- approxfun(time, rep(800, length(time)), rule = 2)


indata <- list(Ww_g = Ww_g, x_shell = 0.002, geom = 3, alpha = alpha, posture = "n",
               Tairf=Tairf, Qsolf=Qsolf, Zenf=Zenf, velf=velf, Tradf=Tradf,
               press=101325, rho_body=932,
               c_body_inner= 3762,k_inner= 0.502,
               c_body_outer=1313 ,k_outer= 0.31)


Tbs_ode <- as.data.frame(ode(y = c(Tc_init=0, Tsk_init=0, Ts_init=0), times = time, func = twolump, parms = indata))


Thank you for the help

Fede

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Constant environment in two-lump
parts:
Hi Fede,

You need to specify all the parameters for this one - that's the reason it's not working.

Incidentally, I submitted the manuscript describing this model and the onelump model yesterday - so hopefully in a few months there will be something to cite! There will be a slight change to the code for these models that will affect the results when metabolic heat is included, but for most ectotherm purposes this can be left at zero for now.

The code below should do what you want:

library(NicheMapR)
library(deSolve)

Ww_g <- 40
alpha <- 0.7

x_shell <- 0.002
geom <- 3
posture <- "n"
press <- 101325
rho_body <- 932
c_body_inner <- 3762
k_inner <- 0.502
c_body_outer <- 1313
k_outer <- 0.31

# define animal parameters - here simulating a 1000 g ellipsoid
c_body <- 3342 # specific heat of flesh, J/kg-C
q <- 0 # metabolic rate, W/m3
orient <- 1 # does the object orient toward the sun? (0,1)
shape_b <- 1/5 # shape coefficient a, -
shape_c <- 1/5 # shape coefficient b, -
shape_coefs <- c(10.4713, 0.688, 0.425, 0.85, 3.798, 0.683, 0.694, 0.743)
fatosk <- 0.4 # solar configuration factor to sky, -
fatosb <- 0.4 # solar configuration factor to substrate, -
emis <- 0.95 # emissivity of skin, -
alpha_sub <- 0.8 # substrate solar absorptivity, -
pdif <- 0.1 # proportion of solar energy that is diffuse, -

time <- seq(0, 3500, 10)
Tradf <-approxfun(time, rep(26, length(time)), rule = 2)
velf <- approxfun(time, rep(0.01, length(time)), rule = 2)
Tairf <- approxfun(time, rep(25, length(time)), rule = 2)
Zenf <- approxfun(time, rep(0, length(time)), rule = 2)
Qsolf <- approxfun(time, rep(800, length(time)), rule = 2)

Tc_init <- 0
Tsk_init <- 0
Ts_init <- 0

indata <- list(Ww_g = Ww_g, x_shell = x_shell, geom = geom, k_inner = k_inner, k_outer = k_outer, q = q, c_body_inner = c_body_inner, c_body_outer = c_body_outer, emis = emis, rho_body = rho_body, alpha = alpha, shape_coefs = shape_coefs, shape_b = shape_b, shape_c = shape_c, posture = posture, orient = orient, fatosk = fatosk, fatosb = fatosb, alpha_sub = alpha_sub, pdif = pdif, press = press)
Tbs_ode <- as.data.frame(ode(y = c(Tc_init, Tsk_init, Ts_init), times = time, func = twolump, parms = indata))
colnames(Tbs_ode) = c("time", "Tc", "Tsk", "Ts", "Tcf")

with(Tbs_ode, plot(Tc ~ time, type = 'l', ylab='Temperature, °C',xlab = 'time', ylim = c(0, 60)))
with(Tbs_ode, points(Ts ~ time, lty = 2, type = 'l', col = '1'))
with(Tbs_ode, points(Tcf ~ time, type = 'l', col = '2'))

All the best,
Mike

Lastly, I have been trying to fiddle with the shell's thermal properties. Thing is setting the conductivity of bone properly is not really possible since the minimum value for the model is 0.4 W/mK while bone gets as low as 0.2 W/mK. Is there any way to set a lower coductivity?

Again, thank you very much for your help.

Best,
Fede

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Constant environment in two-lump
parts:
Hi Fede,

Thanks for pointing this out - the reason is that you're using the lizard geometry for the 2lump model - that option (and the frog/plate/custom) really shouldn't have been left in there as they weren't set up for the 2lump. I've pulled them out now. Also, you hadn't specified every for the onelump model like you had for the twolump, so some default parameters for the onelump model were being used that were different to what you'd set for the twolump sim. I've pasted code below that shows a comparison for onelump, onelump_var and twolump - all very similar (phew!).

All the best,
Mike

p.s. how did you paste in the nicely formatted code in your last post?

library(NicheMapR)
library(deSolve)

#Two_lump
x_shell <- 0.002

geom <- 2
shape_b <- 5
shape_c <- 5

posture <- "n"
orient <- 1 # does the object orient toward the sun? (0,1)
alpha_sub <- 0.9 # substrate solar absorptivity, -
Tc_init <- 15 #initial core temperature (°C)

Tsk_init <- 15 #initial shell (skin) temperature (°C)
Ts_init <- 15 #initial surface temperature (°C)

press <- 101325
rho_body <- 932
fatosk <- 0.4 # solar configuration factor to sky, -
fatosb <- 0.4 # solar configuration factor to substrate, -
pdif <- 0.1 # proportion of solar energy that is diffuse, -
emis <- 0.95 # emissivity of skin
q <- 0 # metabolic rate, W/m3
Ww_g <- 70 #weight
alpha <- 0.2
c_body_inner <- 3762
k_inner <-  0.502
c_body_outer <- 3762
k_outer<- 0.502

Trad <- 21
vel <- 0.1
Tair <- 20
Zen <- 0
Qsol <- 800

time = seq(0, 30000, by = 10)
Tradf <- approxfun(time, rep(Trad, length(time)), rule = 2)
velf <- approxfun(time, rep(vel, length(time)), rule = 2)
Tairf <- approxfun(time, rep(Tair, length(time)), rule = 2)
Zenf <- approxfun(time, rep(Zen, length(time)), rule = 2)
Qsolf <- approxfun(time, rep(Qsol, length(time)), rule = 2)
indata_twolump <- list(Ww_g = Ww_g,

x_shell = x_shell,
               geom = geom,
               k_inner = k_inner,
               k_outer = k_outer,
               q = q,
               c_body_inner = c_body_inner,
               c_body_outer = c_body_outer,
               emis = emis,
               rho_body = rho_body,
               alpha = alpha,
               posture = posture,
               orient = orient,
               fatosk = fatosk,
               fatosb = fatosb,
               alpha_sub = alpha_sub,
               pdif = pdif,

press = press,
               shape_b = shape_b,
               shape_c = shape_c)

Tbs_2l <- as.data.frame(ode(y = c(Tc_init, Tsk_init, Ts_init), times = time, func = twolump, parms = indata_twolump))
colnames(Tbs_2l) = c("time", "Tc", "Tsk", "Ts", "Tcf")

indata_onelump <- list(Ww_g = Ww_g,
               geom = geom,
               k_flesh = k_inner,
               q = q,
               c_body = c_body_inner,

emis = emis,
               rho_body = rho_body,
               alpha = alpha,
               posture = posture,
               orient = orient,
               fatosk = fatosk,
               fatosb = fatosb,
               alpha_sub = alpha_sub,
               pdif = pdif,

press = press,
               shape_b = shape_b,
               shape_c = shape_c)

Tbs_1l_var <- as.data.frame(ode(y = c(Tc_init), times = time, func = onelump_var, parms = indata_onelump))
colnames(Tbs_1l_var) <- c('time', 'Tc', 'Tcf', 'tau', 'dTdt')

#One_lump
Tbs_1l <- as.data.frame(onelump(t = time,
                                Tc_init = 15,
                                Tair = Tair,
                                Qsol = Qsol,
                                Zen = Zen,
                                Trad = Trad,
                                vel = vel,
                                Ww_g = Ww_g,
                                geom = geom,

alpha = alpha,
                                k_flesh = k_inner,
                                c_body = c_body_inner,

shape_b = shape_b,
                                shape_c = shape_c,
                                posture = posture,

rho_body = rho_body,
                                emis = emis,

fatosk = fatosk,
                                fatosb = fatosb,
                                alpha_sub = alpha_sub,
                                pdif = pdif,

press = press,
                                orient = orient,
                                q = q))

#Compare
df <- cbind(two=Tbs_2l, one=Tbs_1l, three=Tbs_1l_var)

with(df, plot(one.Tc ~ time, type = 'l', ylab='Temperature, °C',xlab = 'time', ylim = c(15, 25)))
with(df, points(two.Tc ~ time, type = 'l', col = '2'))
with(df, points(three.Tc ~ time, type = 'l', col = '3'))

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: Constant environment in two-lump
parts:
Hi Fede,

Sorry, you're right, what I said only applies to the one lump model - k_inner and k_outer do affect heat transfer in the two lump model without metabolic heat generation.

I.e. from within the function:
    R_sk <- (x_shell / 2) / (k_outer * ATOT) # resistance of skin
    R_b <- (V_inner ^ (1 / 3)) / (k_inner * ATOT_inner)
    if(geom == 1){
      R_b <- (R - x_shell) / (k_inner * ATOT_inner)
    }
    if(geom == 2){
      R_b <- min(A2, B2, C2) / (k_inner * ATOT_inner)
    }


(like how in inserted that code?)

All the best,
Mike
